simple.meaning: קָלָה (qâlâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to toast , i.e. scorch partially or slowly.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Leviticus, Joshua, Psalms, Jeremiah, beginning at Leviticus 2:14. Its contexts include offering, kingship, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָלָה (H7033).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: קָלָה (qâlâh) / H7033 is traced through Leviticus 2:14, Joshua 5:11, Psalms 38:8, Jeremiah 29:22 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to toast , i.e. scorch partially or slowly
definitions.full: H7033. qalah I. [ קָלָה ] verb roast, parch (Late Hebrew קָלָה id. (rare), קָלִי = Biblical Hebrew; As kalû II. I, III. I burn, consume Meissn Suppl. 84 ; Sabean קלאתם conflagratio, aestus Os 4 ; Os 1 ; Os 19 ; Os 20 CIS iv. No 74, 1.20 ; Arabic fry or roast wheat; Ethiopic burn, fry , so קְלָא ᵑ7 Syriac ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular suffix בָּאֵשׁ קָלָם Jer 29:22 (accusative of person) he roasted them with fire; Passive participle בָּאֵשׁ קָלוּי אָבִיב Lev 2:14 (P) grain parched with fire; so קָלוּי alone, as common food, Josh 5:11 (P), see קָלִי Niph`al Participle נִקְלֶה as noun Psa 38:8 my loins are filled with burning (Vrss Bae with contempt , II. קלה ).
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root (rather identical with 7034 through the idea of shrinkage by heat);

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘If you offer a meal offering of first fruits to Yahweh, you shall offer for the meal offering of your first fruits fresh heads of grain parched with fire and crushed.
They ate unleavened cakes and parched grain of the produce of the land on the next day after the Passover, in the same day.
I am faint and severely bruised.
A curse will be taken up about them by all the captives of Judah who are in Babylon, saying, ‘Yahweh make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire;’
